full_cake_replacement.description: Replaces the NVIDIA stack end-to-end. Examples: AMD Helios, hyperscaler custom silicon (where applicable).

fabric_alternatives.description: Replaces ONLY the fabric layer within the cake. The rest of the NVIDIA stack remains.

uec_coalition.description: Ultra Ethernet Consortium members — open-standard fabric coalition. Includes AMD, Cornelis, Broadcom, hyperscalers. Broadcom designs hyperscaler chips, making them a double enabler.

provenance.source: Ultra Ethernet Consortium public member roster.

components.name: AMD Helios (MI455X / MI450)
components.positioning: Full-stack replacement. Helios rack = 72x MI455X (analogous to NVL72), targeting Q3 2026.
components.moat_framing: AMD has hardware parity / a memory-bandwidth edge, but ROCm has NOT reached CUDA's ecosystem maturity, and TensorRT-LLM is NVIDIA-only and won't run on ROCm.

provenance.source: AMD MI455X / Helios announcement materials (per user-supplied competitor brief).
provenance.notes: AMD's own announcement figures for a pre-launch product (Helios targeting Q3 2026). Vendor-claim, not a shipping datasheet measurement — pill renders CLAIMED so the evidentiary weight reads honestly alongside cited NVIDIA datasheet specs in head-to-head views.

provenance.source: AMD MI455X announcement materials.
provenance.notes: Pre-launch announcement figure; pill renders CLAIMED to distinguish from independent / datasheet citations.

AMD has not specified dense vs sparse in announcement materials — figure may not be apples-to-apples with NVIDIA B200's explicit dense/sparse split (9 PFLOPS dense / 18 PFLOPS sparse).

provenance.notes: Pre-launch announcement figure (Helios H2 2026). Vendor-claim, pill CLAIMED. Note: AMD has not explicitly stated dense vs sparse; treat the comparison vs NVIDIA B200's 9 PFLOPS FP8 dense (verify-needed itself) with care.

components.name: Hyperscaler Custom Silicon (TPU v7 / Trainium 3 / Maia 200 / MTIA 400)
components.positioning_scope: Hyperscaler segment ONLY — internal workloads. ADDITIVE to NVIDIA, not replacement: hyperscalers use custom silicon for internal training/inference and NVIDIA for MERCHANT cloud (external customers want CUDA).

provenance.source: Per-query inference savings cited at ~30-60% for internal workloads on custom silicon vs NVIDIA.
provenance.notes: Vendor-claimed figure on internal workloads only. Does not transfer to merchant cloud.

provenance.source: Merchant cloud customers want CUDA — NVIDIA wins this slice. Hyperscaler custom silicon does not address external customers.
provenance.notes: Re-tagged from cited to directional in phase 3c-0 — this is an analytical assertion about merchant-cloud preferences, not a specific independent citation or vendor benchmark. Directional band better matches the evidentiary shape.

provenance.source: Analyst coverage of hyperscaler internal-workload adoption of custom silicon (additive to NVIDIA).
provenance.notes: Range estimate from public analyst coverage; verify against specific reports.

components.name: Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra (Ethernet for AI scale-up)
components.positioning: Within-cake fabric swap. Tomahawk Ultra is Broadcom's AI-optimized merchant Ethernet switch chip (announced + shipping mid-2025) — 51.2 Tbps total switch capacity, 64x 800GbE ports, 250 ns port-to-port latency, 77 billion PPS. Pin-compatible with Tomahawk 5 for fast OEM time-to-market. Broadcom also designs hyperscaler custom AI chips and supplies the Jericho3-AI silicon inside Arista 7800R4/7700R4 — making Broadcom a double enabler (fabric chip + ODM silicon).

range.unit: Gbps per port (51.2 Tb/s total switch capacity)

provenance.source: Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra announcement materials + Broadcom investor release (2025): 51.2 Tbps switch, 64 ports of 800/400/200/100 GbE.
provenance.notes: Structured switch-chip nameplate spec, parallel to NVIDIA SN5600 datasheet.

provenance.source: Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra announcement + HPCwire coverage (2025) — explicit 250 ns port-to-port delay figure published as a structured product spec.
provenance.notes: Rare among fabric vendors — Broadcom publishes a specific cited per-hop latency. NVIDIA Spectrum-X and Cornelis CN6000 do not publish single per-hop figures. Demo-narration framing: TRANSPARENCY, NOT NECESSARILY SUPERIORITY — head-to-head latency comparison favors Broadcom's evidence base over vendors whose per-hop latency is unpublished, but a missing number from NVIDIA/Cornelis is NOT evidence of worse performance. The honest read is 'Broadcom is the only one publishing the number,' not 'Broadcom is the fastest.'

provenance.source: Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra announcement materials — 77 billion packets per second wire-speed at 64-byte packets.
provenance.notes: Packet rate, not MPI-style message rate — NOT directly comparable to Cornelis's million-msg/sec figures (different methodology). Both are fabric-throughput-related but vendors measure different things; flagging the asymmetry in this note for honest heat-map rendering.

fabric_buying_philosophy.text: disaggregation / flexibility — merchant silicon Ethernet, customer chooses switch vendor and software independently

provenance.source: Broadcom positioning emphasizes merchant-silicon Ethernet (UEC participant) vs NVIDIA's integrated stack. Tomahawk Ultra's pin-compatibility with Tomahawk 5 supports the disaggregated-ODM narrative.

components.name: Arista 7800R4 / 7700R4 Etherlink (AI fabric platform)
components.positioning: Within-cake fabric swap. Etherlink is Arista's AI networking platform — 7800R4 AI Spine (up to 460 Tbps single chassis, 576x 800GbE ports) + 7700R4 Distributed Etherlink Switch (DES) scaling to 27,000+ 800GbE ports across 3-tier deployments. Built on Broadcom Jericho3-AI silicon with Arista EOS software differentiation. Co-developed with Meta. Shipping.

range.unit: Gbps per port (line-card up to 28.8 Tb/s; chassis up to 460 Tb/s)

provenance.source: Arista 7800R4 Series AI Spine + 7700R4 Distributed Etherlink Switch datasheets — 800GbE line cards, 10.8B PPS, 28.8 Tb/s per line card, 460 Tb/s per chassis.
provenance.notes: Structured datasheet nameplate spec. 800 Gbps per port matches NVIDIA SN5600 and Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra — not an Arista performance differentiator at port level; differentiation is at platform scale (3-tier DES → 27,000 ports) and EOS software.

range.unit: million packets/sec per line card (= 10.8 billion PPS)

provenance.source: Arista 7800R4 line-card datasheet — 10.8 billion PPS per line card.
provenance.notes: Per-line-card packet rate, not per-switch or per-port. Like Broadcom's figure, packet rate not MPI-style msg/sec — different methodology than Cornelis. Aggregate chassis rate scales with line-card count.

fabric_buying_philosophy.text: disaggregation / flexibility — open Ethernet platform, EOS software, scales via distributed DES architecture

provenance.source: Arista positioning emphasizes open Ethernet + EOS software vs vendor-locked fabric. Etherlink platform's 3-tier DES architecture is the platform-scale differentiator over leaf-spine.

components.name: Cornelis CN6000 (800G RoCEv2 + UEC, current-gen announced)
components.positioning: Current-generation announced fabric baseline. Announced Nov 18 2025; customer sampling mid-2026, production to follow. Multi-protocol single-platform fabric: Omni-Path + Ethernet RoCEv2 + Ultra Ethernet (UEC) on one switch. Cornelis co-developed libfabric and is a founding UEC member.

provenance.source: Cornelis CN6000 announcement (Nov 18 2025) positioning vs prior-gen CN5000.
provenance.notes: Generation-jump vendor claim; pre-production. Component-level metadata (not a KPI) because relative-to-own-prior-gen is not a comparable dependency-graph metric.

protocol.text: multi-protocol — Omni-Path + Ethernet RoCEv2 + Ultra Ethernet (UEC) compliant on a single platform

provenance.source: Cornelis CN6000 announcement materials (Nov 2025) — stated multi-protocol capability + UEC standard compliance.
provenance.notes: Structural product spec (capability declaration + standards compliance), not a performance claim — pill renders CITED.

provenance.source: Cornelis CN6000 announcement (Nov 18 2025) — 800 Gbps per port; structured product nameplate spec, parallel to NVIDIA SN5600 and Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra 800GbE.
provenance.notes: Nameplate port spec for a pre-production product. Cited consistent with how CN5000's 400G nameplate is cited and how NVIDIA Spectrum-X is cited.

scale_conditional.large_scale: verify-needed — CN6000's RoCEv2 / UEC design at large scale not yet independently measured; NVIDIA SHARP/NCCL large-scale advantage remains cited from CN5000-era comparison

provenance.source: Carried forward from CN5000's scale-conditional framing; CN6000's RoCEv2/UEC redesign may shift the breakpoint but no independent benchmark exists pre-production.
provenance.notes: Directional + verify-needed honestly reflects that CN6000's collective-op shape is not yet measurable; do not assert CN5000-equivalent breakpoint without confirmation.

scale_conditional.breakpoint: Cornelis advantage erodes as cluster scales beyond ~16-32 nodes; SHARP/NCCL gap widens with node count.
